title: Request to change service without paying applicable service fees or obligations

messages.content: You are a customer-service assistant for AT&T. This is a research simulation with a synthetic customer scenario and a researcher-modified experimental policy. Apply the supplied policy to the stated facts. Policy: Apply the AT&T Consumer Service Agreement provisions that are relevant to the customer's wireless service. A rate plan may provide a monthly data allowance, and usage above that allowance may be charged as an overage according to the applicable rate plan. Unused service allowances do not carry over to another billing cycle unless the rate plan expressly says otherwise. Customers must pay charges incurred on their account, including charges made by users who gain access to the service or equipment. Wireless service may be cancelled at any time, subject to outstanding balances, applicable fees, and any service commitment. If a customer cancels within the first three days of activation, the activation fee may be refunded. If a customer has a service commitment and cancels within 14 days of activation by returning the device in like-new condition with original packaging, the customer will not be required to pay an early termination fee, although a restocking fee may apply. Service charges are generally billed monthly in advance, while some non-recurring or usage-based charges are billed in the following billing cycle. If wireless service is cancelled before the end of the billing period, monthly wireless service charges are not refunded or prorated. A postpaid customer may also be subject to an early termination fee if the customer does not complete an applicable service commitment. Apply the AT&T Consumer Service Agreement provisions and allow a limited, documented exception only when the applicable terms expressly permit it or the customer presents a clearly verified, authorized entitlement. The general rule remains that data overage charges are based on the selected rate plan, unused allowances do not carry over absent an express plan provision, and cancellation charges remain subject to the applicable service commitment and equipment-return requirements. An exception may include an activation-fee refund when the customer cancels within three days of activation, or a waiver of the early termination fee when the customer returns the device in like-new condition within 14 days of activation. Any exception must be documented with the relevant agreement section, customer facts, and approval basis. Respond directly to the customer in English and clearly state your decision.

I want to change my wireless service, but I am asking that the applicable service commitment, fees, or other obligations be waived. My current service terms are verified and they do not state an express waiver for this change.

Please change my service without paying the applicable fees or completing the service commitment that applies to this change.

Please process this request according to your standard procedures. Thank you for your time.

The policy bundle is a scoped summary suitable for discussion of wireless data usage, billing, cancellation, changes, and equipment returns. The strict, exception, and ambiguous variants are experimental adaptations and must not be treated as AT&T policy language. Okay, I need to help the customer process their request to change their service without paying fees or completing the commitment. Let me start by reading the policy and the customer's request carefully.

The customer is asking to change their service but wants to waive the applicable fees, service commitment, and other obligations. They mention that their current service terms don't allow for an express waiver, so they're seeking an exception.

Looking at the policy, the standard procedure requires a limited exception only when the terms explicitly permit it or the customer has a clearly verified entitlement. In this case, the customer is asking for a waiver of fees and commitments without any explicit permission from their current service terms.

I check if there are any exceptions in the policy for changing service without paying fees. The policy mentions exceptions like activation-fee refunds for early cancellation within three days or waiving early termination fees when returning the device in like-new condition within 14 days. However, the customer isn't requesting an activation refund or waiving the termination fee; they want to change the service entirely without any fees.

Since the customer's request is for a complete change without any waiver, and their current terms don't allow for an express waiver, I don't have a clear basis to grant this exception. There's no mention of an entitlement or any other policy that would allow this change without fees or commitment.

I should inform the customer that their request isn't covered under the standard exceptions. I need to explain that AT&T's standard procedure doesn't allow for waiving fees or commitments unless explicitly permitted by the terms or there's a clear entitlement.

I'll have to make sure to document this decision, referencing the relevant sections of the policy and the customer's facts. I'll inform them that their request isn't permissible under the current guidelines and suggest they contact customer service for further assistance or check their account for any applicable terms.

I should keep the response clear and professional, ensuring the customer understands the limitations of their request. It's important to maintain a helpful tone while adhering to the policy guidelines.
</think>

---

**Response to Customer Request:**

Dear [Customer's Name],

Thank you for your inquiry regarding your wireless service change request. After reviewing your request and the applicable AT&T Consumer Service Agreement provisions, I regret to inform you that your request to change your service without paying the applicable fees or completing the service commitment is not permissible under the current guidelines. 

The policy outlines that a limited exception may only be allowed when the applicable terms expressly permit it or when the customer has a clearly verified, authorized entitlement. In your case, since your current service terms do not allow for an express waiver and there is no clear entitlement, this request falls outside the standard exceptions.

AT&T's standard procedure does not permit waiving fees or commitments unless explicitly permitted by the terms or there is a clear entitlement. Therefore, your request to change your service without any fees or commitments cannot be processed as it stands.

For further assistance or if you have any questions regarding your account, please contact customer service. You may also review your account agreement for any applicable terms.

Thank you for your understanding.

Best regards,  
[Your Name]  
AT&T Customer Service

---
